# PKCS#12 test files

Every key and certificate here is throwaway material generated by `make.sh` for these tests; none of it protects anything. Regenerate with `./make.sh` (needs OpenSSL 3 with the legacy provider, and python3); the keys change on each run, and the tests compare against the `*.key.der` (PKCS#8) and `*.crt.der` files written alongside. All files use the password `keyroost-test` except `empty-password.p12`. `two-entries.p12`, `ber-indefinite.p12` and `ber-full.p12` are not OpenSSL output: `p12tool.py` joins two single-entry files (recomputing the MAC) and re-wraps `rsa2048-modern.p12` in BER indefinite lengths with a chunked AuthenticatedSafe (the MAC covers bytes that do not change), and `ber-full.p12` goes further (indefinite lengths everywhere, chunked OCTET STRINGs, MAC recomputed), and `make.sh` checks that OpenSSL still opens all three. The two `macless-*` files have no MAC.
